steps.npc: I'm just mining... Problem is, it's a struggle to get past all these fossil looking things.
The others wouldn't like it if a human got involved... You lot tend to take too much from the rocks.

steps.player: But what if I were to sort out these fossil things you mentioned?

steps.npc: Okay, I'll tell you what... If you mine through these calcified deposits, you can keep whatever you get from them.
Yeah, why not. I'm tired of getting sprayed with all the water that leaks from these walls anyway. Not to mention it just brings out lots of extra useless bits with it!

steps.player: So the water makes the walls even more lucrative?

steps.npc: If you consider pointless fossils lucrative, then I suppose.

steps.player: I see. I'll get to work then! See what I can do to help.

options.condition: If the player has blessed bone shards:

steps.text: You show Callio the bone shards.

steps.npc: Bone shards! Totally pointless if you ask me, but I hear the humans up atop the mountain quite like them.
Apparently they offer them up as some sort of sacrifice, but I'm not too sure on the specifics. It's not like I ever go up there myself.

options.text: Can you have a look at this chunk of rock?
options.condition: If the player has a calcified deposit:

steps.player: Can you have a look at this chunk of rock?

steps.text: You show Callio the calcified deposit.

steps.npc: That's quite the chunk indeed. It looks to be a big mass of calcified rock.
I reckon you'll be able to break it up on an anvil. Perhaps there might be something interesting inside...

steps.player: Thanks! I'll go smash it open.

options.condition: If the player has a calcified moth:

steps.npc: Strange... I've never seen one of those before. That's quite the find.

steps.player: Of all the creatures to find stuck in a wall, I didn't expect a moth.

steps.npc: Moths carry a lot of magical power within this mountain. You can probably crush it to consume whatever power is left inside.
Only one way to find out!
